title: Resource tenancy & region-binding — data contract and CRUD patterns
summary: Working notes describing a compact, pragmatic control-plane record shape for resources (tenants, envs, regions, clusters) and the CRUD API behaviors we should standardize on. Focus on region binding semantics, routing policy keys, eventual consistency tradeoffs, and event contract for downstream serving components.
content:
Context and goal:
We need a simple, consistent record contract for control-plane managed entities that makes multi-region routing and cluster binding predictable for the runtime. The goal here is not the final schema; it is a set of concrete fields + API semantics we can iterate on and use to generate event messages, ACL checks, and routing decisions without ambiguous edge-cases.

Primary entities covered in this note:
- Tenant (customer/organization)
- Environment (dev/staging/prod under tenant)
- Region (logical region; maps to cloud region or affinity group)
- Cluster (physical/virtual pool in a region: capacity unit with labels)
- ResourceAssignment (binding of environment -> cluster with routing policy)

Key principles we followed:
1) Flat core identity: every entity has a stable id (uuid), owner_id, created_at, updated_at. Keep the record compact for fast lookups.
2) Declarative bindings: prefer explicit ResourceAssignment records rather than embedding cluster pointers in many places. Assignments are first-class and versioned.
3) Routing keys separation: routing decisions should use a small deterministic keyset (region_hint, cluster_selector_labels, priority). Try not to derive decisions from free-text fields.
4) Event-first: all CRUD operations emit domain events (create/update/delete) with an immutable sequence number for downstream consumers (autoscalers, routers, audit).
5) Opt for last-writer-wins with optimistic concurrency for admin APIs; for high-value operations (reassignments) use gating via two-phase commit-ish workflows (lock token + accept).

Proposed record shapes (minimal):
- Tenant:
  id: uuid
  name: short string
  owner_email: string
  org_slug: short string
  created_at, updated_at (ISO8601)
  billing_plan: string (optional)
  tags: [string] (optional)

- Environment:
  id: uuid
  tenant_id: uuid
  env_key: string (e.g., "prod", "staging", "dev-joe")
  display_name: string
  protection_level: enum {open, restrict-rollout, locked}
  created_at, updated_at

- Region:
  id: uuid
  region_code: string (e.g. "us-west-2", "eu-north-1", "gcp-europe-west2")
  description: string
  allowed_tenants: [tenant_id] or null (null means default allow)
  created_at, updated_at

- Cluster:
  id: uuid
  region_id: uuid
  cluster_key: string (logical name)
  capacity_units: int (nominal throughput units)
  labels: [string] (e.g. ["gpu:v100","zone:a"])
  status: enum {active, draining, offline, provisioning}
  observed_capacity: int (last known)
  created_at, updated_at

- ResourceAssignment (this is the important binding record):
  id: uuid
  environment_id: uuid
  cluster_id: uuid
  region_id: uuid (redundant but useful for fast query)
  priority: int (lower = preferred)
  routing_policy: enum {strict, prefer_local, failover, balanced}
  selector: [string] (label expressions cluster must match, optional)
  effective_from: iso date/time (optional)
  effective_until: iso date/time (optional)
  status: enum {active, pending, retired}
  created_by: user id/email, created_at, updated_at

Why ResourceAssignment?
- Makes rollouts and canary strategies explicit (create pending assignment with lower priority, then flip priorities).
- Supports multi-cluster serving for read replicas or warm standby.
- Avoids embedding cluster pointers in Environment records which cause cross-object churn.

CRUD API patterns
- Use standard REST resources with idempotency keys for create operations. Also support bulk upsert endpoints for batch provisioning.
- All writes require optimistic concurrency: return an ETag header (sha1 of payload + updated_at). Clients must send If-Match to mutate. For non-critical bulk operations allow last-write-wins with warnings.
- Example endpoints (HTTP style):
  POST /v1/tenants -> 201 + {id} (Idempotency-Key header allowed)
  PATCH /v1/tenants/{id} -> 200 (If-Match)
  GET /v1/tenants/{id} -> 200
  GET /v1/tenants?org_slug=acme -> 200

  POST /v1/environments -> 201
  PATCH /v1/environments/{id}

  POST /v1/resource-assignments -> 201 (body must include environment_id + cluster_id + routing_policy)
  PATCH /v1/resource-assignments/{id} -> 200 (change priority/status)
  DELETE /v1/resource-assignments/{id} -> 204 (this emits assignment.deleted event)

Consistency, eventual consistency, and reads
- Control plane authoritative store will be strongly consistent for the CRUD APIs (single region write for the control plane).
- Serving runtime should subscribe to assignment events and reconcile. Downstream caches are eventual. To avoid accidental mismatch during cutover:
  - We emit assignment.created with sequence_number and effective_from. Routers should only apply assignments whose effective_from <= now and whose sequence_number is contiguous or greater than last seen.
  - Provide a /v1/sync endpoint for the runtime to request full snapshot if it detects a gap or misses events (e.g., /v1/snapshots/assignments?since_seq=1234).

Routing decision keys (what runtime uses)
- environment_id (primary)
- region_hint (optional tenant-provided preference)
- assignment priority and routing_policy
- cluster.labels match selector
- cluster.status == active

Routing policy behaviors (proposal):
- strict: only clusters in same region and status active, otherwise failover per configured list
- prefer_local: prefer clusters in hinted region, but allow cross-region with higher cost metric
- failover: route to next priority available cluster (useful for disaster recovery)
- balanced: route across all active clusters according to weights (weight field extension)

Security and multi-tenant considerations
- All APIs include tenant scoping. Cross-tenant assignment is disallowed unless explicit admin override flag is set and recorded in audit log.
- Field-level ACLs: only platform-admins can change region.allowed_tenants; tenant-admins can request assignments only within allowed regions.
- Audit events: every mutation emits an audit event with who, before payload, after payload. These are append-only and immutable.

Event contract (assignment.created example):
{
  "event_type": "assignment.created",
  "sequence_number": "12345",
  "timestamp": "2025-09-10T12:00:00Z",
  "payload": {
    "assignment_id": "uuid",
    "environment_id": "uuid",
    "cluster_id": "uuid",
    "priority": 10,
    "routing_policy": "prefer_local"
  }
}
(Note: above is a conceptual shape; actual event is JSON but not nested in the doc metadata — consumers get this from the events stream.)

Operational patterns and edge cases
- Reassignment race: two admins reassign same env concurrently. We require If-Match + conflict error (409). For quick operational fixes provide a force=true query param that creates a pending assignment and requires manual acceptance.
- Draining clusters: create assignment.status=retired and set effective_until short window; routers should stop sending new sessions to retired assignments but allow existing ones to finish.
- Cross-region latency vs compliance: region.allowed_tenants may be used to enforce data residency. If tenant requests region outside allowed list, API returns 403 with remediation instructions.

Open questions / trade-offs to decide in next sync
- Do we store a small routing weight (0-100) on assignments to enable weighted balanced policy?
- Do we version the routing_policy enum or add a free-form policy blob for future extension? (Pros: flexible; Cons: opaque to platform tools)
- Do we make region->cluster lookup sharded by region_id for the authoritative store to scale reads?

Next actions (concrete)
- Iterate this note into a concise API spec (openapi) with example payloads (owner: Marco) by 2025-09-17.
- Draft event schema with sequence guarantees for serving runtime (owner: Emily) by 2025-09-24.
- Prototype an assignments snapshot endpoint that returns a checksum and high-water sequence number (owner: Jon) by 2025-10-01.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (informal)
- Might be handy: assignment-level annotations for quick flags ("no-autoscale":true) to route maintenance windows.
- Consider a migration tool to convert old env.cluster pointer -> ResourceAssignment records (bulk transform).

References / related docs:
- See platform provisioning RFC (link in linked_artifacts)
- See running-router-notes (infra folder) for how runtime currently consumes cluster metadata

End of working note.
